title: upgrade, on a case-insensitive disk, removes a file devbin renamed only in case after updating it, and overwrites an edit to it unrefused
body:
FOUND 2026-09-23 by vc, reviewing cc's 0123, and DRIVEN by both: vc at 341ded1 plus 0120 plus 0123, and cc in arms red on the same code. The first facet is in lib/cmd/upgrade as it shipped in 0.1.7; 0123 and 0129 carry the same shape into publish and install --force, and are fixed in the same commit.

WHAT HAPPENS. On a case-insensitive disk -- APFS, as macOS formats it, on every machine this fleet runs on -- a case-only rename in devbin's lib/, `Foo` to `foo`, is one file: the copy of `foo` is written into the existing `Foo` entry, and find goes on listing `Foo`. Upgrade compares paths byte for byte, and two things follow.

1. THE FILE JUST UPDATED IS REMOVED. `upgrade --from` a source with the rename prints "updated bin/.devbin/lib/case.d/foo", then retires the recorded `Foo`, which the source no longer ships: "removed bin/.devbin/lib/case.d/Foo (no longer shipped)", rc 0, and `case.d` is left empty. The project has lost a file devbin ships.
2. AN EDIT TO IT IS OVERWRITTEN. The shipped `foo` has no manifest entry, since the manifest recorded `Foo`, so its state reads as `new`, the edited-in-place refusal never fires, and the copy overwrites the project's edit without a word. And had it been refused, a preserved `foo` has no recorded checksum, so manifest_write would record the edit as canonical: issue 0021's laundering.

DRIVEN, cc, in arms: a source shipping lib/case.d/Foo, a project vendored from it, then Foo renamed foo in the source by `git mv` with new content. On the code as it stood, `upgrade --from` printed "removed    bin/.devbin/lib/case.d/Foo"; with the project's copy edited first, no "skipped ... (edited in place" line appeared, and the edit was gone. vc drove the removal the same way, and publish-upgrade and install --force alike.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO. Ask, before removing a path the shipped list lacks, whether it is the same file on this disk as a shipped path under another case (equal ignoring case, then -ef), and if so keep it, renamed to the shipped spelling, and say so. Give a shipped path with no manifest entry the recorded state of its case twin, so an edit is refused as an edit, and carry the twin's recorded checksum forward when it is preserved. One helper for upgrade, publish and install --force, so the three cannot disagree. Arms that run where the disk folds case and skip, naming what they did not check, where it does not; and on a case-sensitive disk, where Foo and foo are two files, the old spelling is still retired.

cc's, built with 0123, 0127 and 0129 in one commit. It ships in 0.1.8 under hv's ruling.

## Resolution

Fixed at c585f3d, in 0123's commit. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. case_twin, in lib/install, answers whether a path the shipped list lacks is, on this disk, a shipped path under another case: equal ignoring case, then -ef. keep_case_twin renames such a path to the shipped spelling and says so. That is one atomic `mv -f` first, checked by what the directory lists, since POSIX lets a rename onto another name for the same file succeed and do nothing. Otherwise it is two checked steps through a mktemp name, with a put-back. remove_unshipped and upgrade's retirement each ask it before removing. Upgrade's copy loop gives a shipped path with no entry its twin's recorded state, so an edit is refused as an edit, and manifest_write carries the twin's checksum forward for a preserved path. On a case-sensitive disk nothing changes: the old spelling is retired.
- DRIVEN. vc drove a case-only rename, Foo to foo, through publish, install --force and upgrade, intact and edited, on a case-folding disk. Every path kept the file under the new spelling. The edited copy was refused and kept, and its manifest row still carries the old checksum, so doctor flags the edit. The case-sensitive control ran on an APFS case-sensitive image.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. The four case arms were red on the first version sent for review. Y1-Y5, Y7b, Y7d, Y8 and Y9 were killed, rerun on the final version with the same verdicts. Y3 is killed on the image, and Y7a is an exercise.
- THE SUITE. As 0123's resolution: 1..1694, 1694 ok, 0 not ok, 5 expected skips, rc 0.
